value: best hearing frequency 4 kHz within the 1 to 8 kHz range tested, mean audiogram of saline-injected control gerbils (ABR audiometry, n = 18)
method: auditory brainstem response audiometry: pure tones 1 to 8 kHz presented at 30 to 90 dB SPL in 5 dB steps, response taken as RMS amplitude over 0 to 10 ms, thresholds estimated automatically
conditions: Laboratory; 10-week-old male gerbils (37 used in the study, 18 in the saline control group); audiograms averaged across the time points (pre, 20 min and 2 h after saline injection) in an acoustic chamber; anaesthetised with ketamine and medetomidine (with atropine)

source.authors: Lanaia V, Tziridis K, Schulze H
source.title: Salicylate-Induced Changes in Hearing Thresholds in Mongolian Gerbils Are Correlated With Tinnitus Frequency but Not With Tinnitus Strength

where: Results, subsection The Hearing Threshold in the Control Group (Fig. 2A left panel)
quote: The Figure 2A left panel shows the mean audiogram (factor frequency) averaged across the different time points in control gerbils, with the best hearing frequency at 4 kHz.
note: The tested range stops at 8 kHz, so 4 kHz is the best frequency within 1 to 8 kHz and not the species' best frequency overall; thresholds were not tabulated per frequency in the text (frequency-averaged control mean 38.45 +/- 13.45 dB SPL before and 32.94 +/- 12.72 dB SPL 2 h after saline, a significant fall with time). The same paper's salicylate group (300 mg/kg) had slightly higher thresholds at 2 h (39.51 vs 32.94 dB SPL, p = 0.002) that were back to baseline after a week, and thresholds were measured alongside a startle-based tinnitus assay, which is not filed here. Name Meriones unguiculatus is listed as accepted in docs/views/gaps/gbif-names.tsv. Crossref licence CC BY 4.0 and the PDF states CC BY. No statistical test of the frequency effect is reported; the authors state that gerbil hearing up to 20 kHz resembles the human audiogram with best hearing around 4 kHz (citing Ryan 1976).
